title: COP31, global warming projections and other nature news | World Economic Forum
gist: Ahead of COP31 in Antalya (9-20 November), UNEP's Emissions Gap Report projects 2.8°C warming under current policies (2.6°C with full pledges) and declares 1.5°C overshoot unavoidable, with pledges delivering only 11-15% emission cuts by 2035 versus the 45% needed. The roundup also covers COP17's Yerevan Pathway on biodiversity, record 426.8 ppm CO2, a 36% rise in heat deaths, record-low Amazon deforestation, and persistent adaptation-finance gaps.

themes.theme: UNEP emissions gap and warming trajectory

insights.claim: UNEP's 2026 Emissions Gap Report projects 2.8°C of warming this century under current policies, and 2.6°C even if countries fully implement their current climate pledges.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Policy-path baseline is far above Paris targets, implying sustained regulatory and physical-risk pressure on carbon-intensive assets.
insights.quote: The world could warm by 2.8°C this century if current climate policies continue
insights.locator: 1. COP31 approaches as UN warns of 2.8°C warming

insights.claim: UNEP's report 'The Point of Return' states that exceeding the Paris Agreement's 1.5°C threshold is now unavoidable; the policy question has shifted to how far and how long temperatures overshoot.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Climate discourse is pivoting from prevention to overshoot management and adaptation, favouring adaptation spending themes.
insights.quote: warns that exceeding the Paris Agreement's 1.5°C warming threshold is now unavoidable
insights.locator: The report, The Point of Return

insights.claim: To stay on a 1.5°C-consistent pathway, global greenhouse gas emissions would need to fall 18% by 2030, 45% by 2035 and 69% by 2040 versus 2025 levels, whereas full implementation of current national pledges cuts emissions only 11-15% by 2035.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: The roughly 30-point gap between required and pledged cuts by 2035 signals that pledge-based decarbonisation demand forecasts are overstated relative to targets.
insights.quote: global greenhouse gas emissions would need to fall by 18% by 2030, 45% by 2035 and 69% by 2040, compared with 2025 levels
insights.locator: The scale of the challenge is significant.

insights.claim: New UN climate assessments find governments increasingly integrating climate action into economic planning, though significant gaps remain between national commitments and the action required.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Climate policy is becoming embedded in fiscal and industrial planning even as ambition lags.
insights.quote: governments are increasingly integrating climate action into economic planning
insights.locator: For delegates at COP31, the question

insights.claim: COP31 takes place in Antalya, Türkiye, from 9 to 20 November 2026, with governments focused on accelerating emissions reductions, adaptation and climate finance.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Near-term headline catalyst for climate finance and emissions policy announcements.
insights.quote: taking place in Antalya, Türkiye, from 9 to 20 November
insights.locator: The findings come ahead of the UN Climate

insights.claim: The first global review under the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework found the world off track to meet its 23 biodiversity targets by 2030.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Biodiversity targets are slipping, raising odds of tighter nature-related regulation and disclosure later.
insights.quote: found the world is off track to meet its 23 biodiversity targets by 2030
insights.locator: The agreement comes after the first global review

insights.claim: The 'Yerevan Pathway', adopted at COP17 in Armenia on 31 October, calls for faster national biodiversity plan implementation, reform of nature-harming subsidies and incentives, and more financial and technical support for developing countries; nearly $2 billion in new biodiversity funding was announced.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Subsidy reform targeting nature-harming incentives could affect agriculture, fishing and extractive sectors that rely on them.
insights.quote: reforms to subsidies and other incentives that harm nature
insights.locator: Adopted at the conclusion of the summit

insights.claim: The biodiversity framework commits to conserving 30% of the world's land and waters and putting at least 30% of degraded ecosystems under effective restoration by 2030, but significant financing gaps remain.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: 30x30 conservation targets imply land-use constraints and a funding need that private nature finance is expected to fill.
insights.quote: conserve 30% of the world's land and waters and bring at least 30% of degraded ecosystems under effective restoration by 2030
insights.locator: The framework includes commitments to conserve

insights.claim: Global atmospheric CO2 reached 426.8 ppm in 2025, about 53% above pre-industrial levels, per the World Meteorological Organization, with methane and nitrous oxide also at records.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Record GHG concentrations lock in further warming regardless of near-term policy, sustaining physical-risk pricing.
insights.quote: Global atmospheric carbon dioxide concentrations reached 426.8 parts per million in 2025, around 53% above pre-industrial levels

insights.claim: The 2026 Lancet Countdown finds average annual heat-related deaths rose nearly 36% in the decade after the Paris Agreement versus the prior decade; heat contributed to 710,000 deaths in 2023, over 70% attributable to human-caused climate change.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Rising heat mortality strengthens the case for adaptation spending and health-system climate costs.
insights.quote: heat contributed to 710,000 deaths globally in 2023, with more than 70% attributable to human-caused climate change
insights.locator: Heat-related deaths rise as climate risks grow

insights.claim: Deforestation in Brazil's Amazon fell 42% in the year to July 2026 to its lowest level on record, with about 3,335 square kilometres lost, according to official figures reported by Reuters.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: A rare positive datapoint that supports Brazil's credibility in forest-carbon and nature finance markets.
insights.quote: Deforestation in Brazil's Amazon rainforest fell by 42% in the year to July 2026, reaching its lowest level on record
insights.locator: Amazon rainforest deforestation falls to record low

insights.claim: The ocean absorbs about 30% of human-caused CO2 emissions and 90% of excess heat, but warming and degradation are stressing these sinks; a UN report calls for more investment in ocean monitoring, modelling and data.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Weakening ocean sinks would accelerate warming beyond model baselines; ocean data infrastructure is an emerging funding area.
insights.quote: The ocean absorbs around 30% of human-caused carbon dioxide emissions and 90% of excess heat
insights.locator: UN calls for stronger ocean carbon monitoring

insights.claim: A UN Climate Change assessment finds 81 developing countries have submitted national adaptation plans, but many struggle to secure finance and implement them.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Adaptation finance, not planning, is the binding constraint; expect it to be a central COP31 negotiation item.
insights.quote: 81 developing countries have submitted national adaptation plans, but many face difficulties securing finance
insights.locator: Climate adaptation plans face funding barriers

insights.claim: The Green Climate Fund approved two FAO-supported projects worth $184.8 million in Algeria and Mexico for sustainable forest management, land restoration and climate-resilient agriculture, expected to benefit over one million people.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Multilateral climate funds remain an active channel for adaptation-oriented agriculture capital.
insights.quote: The Green Climate Fund has approved two FAO-supported projects worth $184.8 million in Algeria and Mexico

themes.theme: Blue finance and Indigenous conservation funding

insights.claim: The ocean supports more than 100 million jobs worldwide, yet many sustainable ocean projects struggle to attract investment; WEF's 'Catalytic Blue Finance' report explores financing models and partnerships to unlock commercial capital.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Blended/catalytic structures are being pitched as the route to scale private capital into ocean economy assets.
insights.quote: The ocean supports more than 100 million jobs worldwide, yet many sustainable ocean projects struggle to attract investment
insights.locator: How can blue finance support a sustainable ocean economy?

insights.claim: Indigenous Peoples manage vast areas critical to biodiversity and climate stability but receive only a small share of conservation funding; more direct, locally led finance is argued to improve conservation outcomes.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Conservation finance allocation may be inefficient relative to who actually stewards high-value ecosystems.
insights.quote: receive only a small share of conservation funding
insights.locator: Why are Indigenous Peoples still underfunded
